observed_failure.reason: The old split-transaction near miss necessarily calls begin and commit twice on fault-free success. That violates the frozen normative rule 'Begin exactly once' and the publicly observable callback trace, so it cannot be a singleton near miss.

supersedes_only.old_counterexample: stage_receipt raises after channel/event staging: exact 503 and all three public views equal pre-state.
supersedes_only.new_counterexample: Five fresh subprobes inject stage_receipt failure after channel/event staging; five fresh subprobes inject the first commit failure after all three stages. Every subprobe returns exact 503 and all three public views equal pre-state.
supersedes_only.old_near_miss: Split receipt transaction: commit channel+event in T1 and receipt in T2.
supersedes_only.new_near_miss: On stage_receipt StoreError only, incorrectly commit the active transaction and return storage_failure; all other StoreErrors still roll back. It is fault-free equivalent, uses one transaction, and fails only release_failure_atomicity. The planned mutant commits rather than rolls back for every StoreError, so the commit-failure subprobes distinguish it: planned mutant retries commit and persists all three records, while the near miss rolls back after the injected commit failure.
supersedes_only.planned_mutant_unchanged: Unconditionally commit rather than rollback in StoreError handler.

unchanged: all three replacement candidate IDs and families
all public interfaces and normative success behavior
